result.summary: The image shows a residential intersection with row houses, featuring basic pedestrian infrastructure like sidewalks and a marked crosswalk. While traffic lights are present, the environment lacks high-visibility markings and dedicated pedestrian signals, and sightlines are partially obstructed by a large vehicle.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Large Vehicle
hazards.description: A large black pickup truck is positioned very close to the intersection, blocking sightlines between pedestrians and oncoming traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground, left side of the frame.

hazards.name: Low Visibility Crosswalk
hazards.description: The crosswalk uses standard parallel line markings which are less visible to drivers than high-visibility continental patterns.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces near the intersection to ensure clear sightlines for both drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Upgrade the existing crosswalk to a continental or ladder pattern to increase its visibility to approaching motorists.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to shorten the pedestrian crossing distance and improve the visibility of pedestrians waiting to cross.

result.summary: The intersection features high-visibility crosswalks and bollard-protected curb extensions that improve pedestrian visibility and shorten crossing distances. However, the lack of visible pedestrian signals and a physical median refuge are notable deficiencies in an otherwise well-marked residential environment.

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian signals
hazards.description: No pedestrian signal heads are visible at this signalized intersection, which can lead to confusion for pedestrians about when it is safe to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the intersection near the traffic light pole.

hazards.name: Unprotected crossing distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross the entire width of the roadway without a median refuge, increasing exposure to traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the roadway at the crosswalk.

interventions.title: Install Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Add dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear information to people crossing.

interventions.title: Concrete Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Replace the flexible bollards with permanent concrete curb extensions to further shorten crossing distance and prevent illegal parking.

result.summary: The image shows a narrow urban street with mixed commercial and residential land use. While sidewalks are present on both sides, the intersection lacks marked crosswalks, traffic control devices, and curb ramps, requiring pedestrians to cross unprotected.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: Lack of marked crosswalks at the intersection increases the risk of pedestrian-vehicle conflicts.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles close to the corner obstruct the view between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right and left curbs near the intersection

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at the corners to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the intersection to improve sightlines.

result.summary: The intersection features marked zebra crosswalks, pedestrian signals, and a bike lane protected by flexible bollards. While basic infrastructure is present, sightlines are significantly obstructed by parked vehicles and a large truck in the immediate foreground, increasing risk at the crossing.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Parked cars along the right curb line block the view between approaching drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the roadway beyond the crosswalk

hazards.name: Large Vehicle Obstruction
hazards.description: A large black truck in the immediate foreground significantly obscures the crossing area and sightlines for anyone entering the roadway from the right.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to improve visibility between pedestrians and motorists.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten the crossing distance and improve pedestrian visibility.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signal to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before the parallel vehicle traffic gets a green light.
